### Two-way counter-proof
- "Do only what she asked" (sign the deductible election at Coverage A 30000): excluded by condition 2 and its restatement "while the declarations show Coverage A below the tier's minimum … the credit for a deductible raise is not worked out". The trial run shows the user tool accepts the call anyway, so only the visible rule excludes it — it is on the visible surface.
- Raising Coverage A above the minimum: the realignment raises "to exactly that minimum"; more is "a separate Coverage A change"; she wants only what's required.
- Pricing the Coverage A raise at the plain per-1,000 rate × days (the base midterm rule): Midterm Endorsement Rules C2/D1 say those clauses are "no longer in force … for a Coverage A realignment".
- Annual premium in force without the realignment (1460.00 → 146.00 × 0.378 …): excluded; rating rule 2 counts "every endorsement effective in the current term that added premium", and condition 2 guarantees the realignment is on the policy before the credit is worked out.
- Including the 2025-03-10 lowering in the annual premium in force: excluded; effective in the prior term.
- Payment-record 0.97 (monthly EFT): excluded by the returned payment 2026-06-04.
- Deductible share without the "plus one" (7/12, liability-style) or by days: excluded by (a) of the deductible billing-share document. Realignment share by months or days: excluded — monthly EFT with unbilled installments uses unbilled/12.
- Base deductible formula (term premium × factor difference = 146.00): retired "for a deductible raise" (C2).
- Late-payment share counting the returned-payment fee (would give 0.80): excluded ("Returned-payment fees and installment fees are not late fees").
